text:
maya: FYI saw a sharp p99 OOM spike after the kernel-routing change on the 1.5B inference fleet. stacktrace looked like allocator thrash + kvcache warmup.
maya: summary: before change p99 memory ~6.2GB, after change bursts to ~8.7GB and we hit OOM on some canaries :confused: :eyes:
maya: profiler snippet:
```
Malloc calls: 312k
Peak GPU mem: 8.7 GB
Workspace high-water: 2.1 GB
KV-cache live: ~1.8 GB
Allocatable fragmentation: 18%
GC cycles triggered: 4 -> 12
```
maya: current config on the canary (pytorch/CUDA allocator knobs):
```
expandable_segments: true
max_split_size_mb: 32
garbage_collection_threshold: 0.7
```
liam: thanks — can you paste the exact command/trace for repro? are we seeing this only with batching enabled?
maya: repro-ish command (runs the model locally with same inputs):
```
python -m run_infer --model 1.5B --seq-len 1024 --batch 8 --kernel-routing v2 --kvwarmup 1
```
maya: quick observation: toggling `max_split_size_mb` to 64 reduced peak to ~7.0GB and avoided the OOM in my local run. that suggests split-size interaction with the new kernel selection.
anya: interesting. could be that smaller max_split_size causes more tiny allocations -> more fragmentation with the new kernel packing. can you try raising `garbage_collection_threshold` to 0.85 and see if GC timing helps?
liam: also check whether our batching heuristic is forcing larger workspace reservations when kernel routing prefers specialized attention kernels. that could blow the workspace footprint.
jordan: agree with anya. another quick experiment: try `expandable_segments=false` and `max_split_size_mb=128` — if that stabilizes it, we know fragmentation + split behavior is the root cause.
maya: running the three quick experiments now, will post numbers. initial run (baseline) attached logs: `p99 8.7GB`, toggled max_split_size=64 -> `p99 7.1GB`, set gc_threshold=0.85 -> `p99 7.5GB`, set expandable_segments=false & max_split_size=128 -> `p99 6.4GB` :thumbsup:
anya: nice — that last config looks promising. but we should test at scale; local runs are helpful but canary is the real signal.
liam: can we do a small canary rollout with the `expandable_segments=false, max_split_size_mb=128` config and keep kernel-routing v2? also include a fallback that reverts after 30m if errors > 0.5%.
maya: will prepare the canary. posting the rollout plan next.
ops-bot: deploybot: Canary rollout started for service=runtime-v2, id=canary-2025-08-21-01 :information_source:
liam: if canary shows reduced OOMs, we should consider making this the default for models in the 1B-3B band until we rewrite the allocator to better coalesce splits.
jordan: file an RFC for allocator-side defragmentation + a tuning dashboard for these knobs. track per-model recommended defaults.
maya: noted. I'll attach the perf traces and a short script to reproduce to the canary ticket. thanks all :heart:
ops-bot: deploybot: Canary update: 5/50 hosts reporting OOMs (was 12/50) — continuing monitoring :bar_chart:
